subject.summary: Neuschwanstein Castle above the Pöllat gorge, Schwangau, Bavaria: the five-storey Palas with its 65 m northern stair tower, the Knights' House, the 45 m square tower, the Bower and the east-facing gatehouse, massed from the traced ground plan and the north elevation, on a sketched rock ridge.

identity.feature: Palas: tall five-storey block under a steep slate roof, gabled at both ends (knight west, lion to the court)
Northern stair tower, the tallest (65 m): corbelled gallery, narrower upper drum, crown, spire
Slender stair turret beside the north tower's drum
Southern stair tower before the south front, crenellated crown and spire
Four corbelled, spired corner turrets on the Palas
Paired round-arched windows on five storeys, the Singers' Hall arcade (storey 4), cornice and lesenes on the Palas fronts
Dormers in two rows and pinnacled stacks on the Palas roof
Two-storey Söller loggia on the west front
Chair tower (pyramid roof) and glazed conservatory on the north front
Knights' House, gabled to the north, with its round crenellated turret
Gallery with blind arcades linking the Knights' House and the square tower
Square tower (45 m): pointed openings at the top, corbelled platform, round crenellated lookout and cap
Gatehouse facing east: round-arched gate under stepped gables, two round crenellated corner towers
Bower (Kemenate) on the south of the upper court with two pyramid-roofed towers
Towers and turrets, counted: 14, each at its own height
Two courts on two levels and the crenellated wall on the cliff edge; the castle on its rock ridge

next: Deeper crag: the main-elevation photo shows forest below the castle, so rock deeper than this stepped wedge shows under the north front and fails compare (3 m more: IoU 0.84 to 0.76). A far photo with the cliff visible would allow full depth.
Critics disagreed on the north tower's gallery height and the storey-4 windows; both were settled by measuring the Marienbruecke photo (grouped lights; short drum, spire about 2.5x the drum).
The plan turns the Palas west block about 8-10 degrees; it is drawn here as one orthogonal block.
In x-ray occlusion the far-face windows print through the near fronts at 24%; a depth fade per part would clear the doubled grids.
Gable figures (knight, lion) are stacked primitives; traced silhouettes would read better.
